method_card.title: Circle Theorems
method_card.content:
Every circle theorem starts from a picture. Draw in radii to make isosceles triangles, and look for a diameter, which gives a 90° angle in a semicircle.

The workhorse fact is that the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc. Halve to go inward, double to go outward.
method_card.example:
Angle at centre = 110°. Find the angle at the circumference.

Circumference = \(110 \div 2 = 55°\) (the centre is twice the circumference).

steps: Add every fact you can: radii make isosceles triangles, diameters make 90° angles in a semicircle.
Work from what you know to the centre angle, then halve for the circumference.
If letters appear, build one equation in x, solve, then substitute back.
gold.title: Gold: chain the theorems

example.question: O is the centre. Angle OAB = 40°. Find angle ACB (C on the major arc).

steps: Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc: halve to go in, double to go out.
Semicircle: the angle in a semicircle is 90°. Same segment: angles on the same chord are equal.
Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles add to 180°. A tangent meets a radius at 90°, and two tangents from a point are equal.

For the alternate segment, the tangent-chord angle equals the angle in the alternate segment.
Solve the short equation, then substitute back to check.

guided_steps.say: Two theorems combine. Alternate segment: the angle in the alternate segment equals the tangent-chord angle. Then the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.

guided_steps.hint: They are equal by the alternate segment theorem.

misconceptions.message: First the alternate segment angle equals the tangent-chord angle, 65°. Then the angle at the CENTRE is twice that: 2 × 65 = 130°. Stopping at 65 forgets the centre step.

gold.hint: Opposite angles sum to 180; form an equation in x and solve.

misconceptions.message: Opposite angles SUM to 180, they are not equal. 4x + 2x + 30 = 180 gives x = 25. Setting 4x = 2x + 30 gives x = 15.

gold.hint: It links a tangent-chord angle to an angle in the far segment.
gold.display: The angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment, the angle at the circumference on the other side of the chord. Which theorem is this?

misconceptions.message: Tangent-radius is about the 90° between a tangent and a radius. This links a tangent-chord angle to the alternate segment, so it is the alternate segment theorem.

gold.hint: Use the equal radii to find the centre angle, then halve it.

Angle at the circumference is half the centre: 128 ÷ 2 =

gold.hint: The semicircle gives a 90 degree angle at C; then use the triangle sum.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accurately AB is a diameter of the circle. C is on the circle. Angle CAB = \(34°\). Find angle ABC.

guided_steps.say: AB is a diameter, so angle ACB stands in a semicircle and equals 90°. Then use the triangle.

guided_steps.pre: Triangle ACB adds to 180. Add the two known angles: 90 + 34 =

misconceptions.message: 90° is angle ACB (the semicircle right angle), not the angle asked. Put it in the triangle: 180 − 90 − 34 = 56°.

guided_steps.say: AB is a diameter, so C sits in a semicircle.

guided_steps.pre: A diameter is a straight line. How many degrees is a straight line?
The angle in the semicircle is half of that: 180 ÷ 2 =
So angle ACB is a right angle. Type it:
guided_steps.done: 90°, and it is 90° wherever C sits on the arc.

misconceptions.message: A diameter is a straight line (180°), but the angle at C on the circle is half of that. The angle in a semicircle is 90°.

They are equal, and one is 48°, so x =

misconceptions.message: Angles in the same segment are equal, not supplementary. They stand on the same chord, so x = 48°.

bronze.hint: The angle in a semicircle is always a right angle.

They are equal, and one is 55°, so x =

misconceptions.message: A radius goes from the centre to the circumference, only half way. A chord through the centre reaches both sides, so it is a diameter.

silver.hint: The tangent meets the radius at 90 degrees; the chord splits that right angle.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately A tangent touches the circle at A. The angle between the tangent and chord AB is \(50°\). OA is a radius. Find the angle between the chord AB and the radius OA.

guided_steps.say: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius, so the tangent-radius angle is 90°. The chord AB splits it into two parts.

guided_steps.pre: The whole angle between tangent and radius is:
guided_steps.hint: Tangent meets radius at a right angle.

guided_steps.pre: Check the two parts rebuild the right angle: 50 + 40 =
guided_steps.done: Back to 90°, so the chord-radius angle is 40°.

misconceptions.message: The tangent-radius angle is 90°, split into the tangent-chord part (50°) and the chord-radius part. So chord-radius = 90 − 50 = 40°, not 50.

silver.hint: Double for the centre angle, then take it from 360 degrees for the reflex.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately C is on the major arc. The angle at the circumference, angle ACB, is \(40°\). Find the reflex angle at the centre, angle AOB.

guided_steps.say: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference. Then the reflex angle is the rest of the full turn of 360°.

guided_steps.done: A full 360°, so the reflex angle is 280°.
guided_steps.hint: The two centre angles make a full turn.

misconceptions.message: The (non-reflex) centre angle is 2 × 40 = 80°. The REFLEX angle is the rest of the full turn: 360 − 80 = 280°.
Double the circumference angle first: 2 × 40 = 80°, then reflex = 360 − 80 = 280°. Using 360 − 40 = 320 forgets to double.

silver.hint: The three angles of the triangle add to 180; one of them is 90.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accurately AB is a diameter, so angle ACB = \(90°\). The other two angles of triangle ABC are \(x\) at A and \(2x\) at B. Find \(x\).

guided_steps.say: Angle ACB is 90° (angle in a semicircle). The three angles of the triangle add to 180°.

guided_steps.hint: What the other two angles must share.

guided_steps.pre: The other two are x and 2x, so x + 2x = how many x?

misconceptions.message: Do not forget the 90° angle. All three add to 180: 90 + x + 2x = 180, so 3x = 90 and x = 30. Ignoring the 90 gives x = 60.
